newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Afribrand rekindles earlier buy talks.
newsitem.headline: Afribrand rekindles earlier buy talks.

text.p: Afribrand Holdings, a South African lower-income confectionary to snacks firm which listed on the Johannesburg market on Tuesday, said it had rekindled talks on an acquisition which started earlier this year.

Afribrand, which began trading at a 100 percent premium to its issue price in hectic dealings and continued to surge on Wednesday, earlier issued a cautionary notice saying it was in unspecified talks.
"We had one or two discussions and then the prospectus came out and then we had to stop. We are bringing our discussions back again," Stephen Weir, Afribrand's chief executive, told Reuters.

He declined to say how many possible purchases the firm was eyeing, but squashed market rumours that it could be as many as 20. He said it was hoped that discussions would be finalised in the next couple of weeks.
Weir said that with the share currently running at a forward price earnings ratio of around 30, the funding of possible purchases was not of concern.
"Size for us is not an issue, same market, same kind of product range," he said.

Afribrand said last month that in choosing acquisitions, it would continue to focus on its core operations of supplying food products to the lower income market, but it would also consider other informal sector opportunities.
A food analyst said that Afribrand may have up to three acquisitions, at least one of which may be big enough to double the firm's market capitalisation.

"The one firm they may be looking at buying has turnover of around 18 million rand ($3.8 million)," the analyst said, adding that although Afribrand had cash available for acquisitions it may have to issue shares to fund it.

Afribrand has forecast a 41 percent surge in earnings per share to 9.4 cents for the year to end-May 1998 and a dividend of 2.4 cents. An earnings jump of 26 percent and a dividend of 3.0 cents is predicted for 1999.
Shares touched a 280 cents high earlier, and by 1120 GMT were trading 50 cents up on the day at 276 cents on volume of over 6.5 million stocks.
